to say no those are just the apostates those  are people who were doing what they knew they   were not supposed to be doing problem with that  is that the only text in the Hebrew Bible that
have a problem at all with worshiping Asherah  are dated by critical scholars to the period
of the deuteronomistic literature or later and  that suggests that this condemnation of Asherah
began as a part of Josiah's project of cult  centralization which was intended to centralize
all the worship in the area around the one temple  in Jerusalem and the one patron deity of Israel
under the one priesthood that was located there  in Jerusalem and this was likely an attempt to
programmatize institutionalize this de facto cult  centralization that arose after Sennacherib had
come through at the end of the 8th century and  destroyed all the other cult sites in the area   except for the temple in Jerusalem and Josiah  was probably reacting against attempts by kings
between Hezekiah and Josiah to restore that  worship and a part of that was rewriting a
lot of the histories to make it seem like all  those kings who were engaged in what was then   considered perfectly normal worship were doing  what they knew they were not supposed to be doing
